text:
alia: quick brain dump — sketching a small polymorphic hosting runtime shim that negotiates capabilities at probe time and lets us keep a single public API across hosted/dedicated/private. thinking this reduces special-casing in callers while keeping runtime-specific optimizations behind a capability manifest.

mike: curious — what does 'negotiate capabilities at probe time' look like in practice? sounds like extra round trips.

alia: good question. not per token — probe only on first attach / new model version. runtime returns a compact manifest that we cache (TTL + invalidation). runtime manifest example: 
```json
{"contract_version":"v1alpha2","capabilities":["kv_cache","continuous_batching","streaming","quantized_exec"],"limits":{"max_seq":4096,"max_batch_size":64},"fallbacks":{"streaming":"polling"}}
```

kevin: how do we handle auth/secret handoff for private deployments? we've had awkward rebind flows before.

alia: two parts — control-plane handshake issues and per-request auth. handshake: ephemeral control tokens from customer-managed KMS to verify control-plane probe. per-request: we carry a minimal `runtime-origin` envelope that lets runtime map to tenant secrets (no long-lived keys in control-plane). if runtime doesn't support that, it replies `capabilities` without `secret_rebind` and we fall back to sidecar proxy.

sophia: observability concerns — need consistent trace IDs and cost attribution across modes. can't have different telemetry shapes per mode.

danielle: agree. proposal: manifest includes `telemetry_envelope` schema and runtime must accept `x-rw-origin` header. runtime should emit cost/tokens as structured tags so console can unify metrics.

mike: performance worry — manifest fetch + parsing might add jitter on cold paths.

alia: mitigate: (1) manifest is tiny and cached; (2) fast-path uses manifest cache, with refresh async; (3) we allow an explicit `prefer-fast-path` header that bypasses probe if caller knows runtime shape (useful for hot flows).

kevin: rollback/compat story? some runtimes (older dedicated clusters) won't speak v1alpha2.

alia: manifest includes `contract_version` and a `compat` map. control-plane will maintain adaptors for older clusters (translate older flags into v1alpha2 view). adaptors live in the routing plane, not callers. fallback policy will include explicit feature-gating for security-sensitive capabilities.

infra-bot: FYI — probe-first logic will require a minor LB rule change to allow 204 responses for health+manifest.

deploy-bot: canary pushed to staging with a basic manifest negotiation shim — https://ci/repo/12345 (staging), no perf regressions observed in 10k req smoke. :eyes:

mike: nice. can we include a small micro-benchmark plan in RFC? e.g., cold-probe latency, warm-path impact, and failure-mode SLO tests.

alia: yes — will include benchmark matrix and a migration plan: probe-opt-in flag, adaptor for legacy clusters, and an emergency `force-mode` header that disables negotiation for critical paths.

sophia: +1 to telemetry envelope and `origin` header. also add a regression alert in Optimize tied to a canonical prompt set so we catch quality regressions when adaptors translate features.

kevin: +1 but also call out secret lifecycle (rotate/evict) — we should define eviction semantics in the manifest.

danielle: +1, and document the observability fields we'll require. ops needs those to reconcile per-tenant billing.

alia: great — next steps: I'll draft an RFC with the manifest schema, adaptor semantics, probe caching rules, and the fallback table (sidecar, adaptor, force-mode). aiming for draft by EOW. flag if you want to be a reviewer.

kevin: I'll review. mike + sophia too?

mike: happy to.

sophia: add me.

deploy-bot: canary note: staging run used `contract_version=v1alpha2` and `prefer-fast-path=false`. logs: https://ci/logs/12345

alia: thanks — adding reviewers and writing RFC. will ping when draft is up. :+1:
